title: Patient Care Desk Guidance: Plan Bridge Days on Lost-or-Stolen Prescriptions Replacements
content:
A lost-or-stolen replacement of a Kestrel Prescriptions record carries the theft replacement plan bridge according to the patient's active prescription coverage under Prescription Insurance on File and the claims that plan has paid.

## The rule

The theft replacement plan bridge looks at the patient's active prescription coverage and its paid claims for the prescription:

- a plan allowing **at least one** lost-or-stolen override a plan year that has paid **three or more** claims for the prescription in the last 12 months adds **3 days**;
- such a plan with **one or two** paid claims for the prescription adds **1 day**;
- any other case adds nothing.

These days are added to the lost days remaining after any restraint, before the days covered by a corrected remake are taken off; the theft replacement days supply is never below zero and is taken down to whole days.

## Combinations (hypothetical active plans)

| Lost-or-stolen overrides the plan allows a plan year | Claims paid for the prescription in the last 12 months | Days added |
|---|---|---|
| 1 or more | 3 or more | 3 |
| 1 or more | 1 or 2 | 1 |
| 1 or more | 0 | nothing |
| 0 | any | nothing |
| no active plan | — | nothing |

**Which claims count?** Paid claims for the same prescription in the last 12 months, as logged against the coverage.
